To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the contact-interaction limits on Λ are 50–80 TeVs for LHC and 13–15 TeVs for SSC, if the angular distributions of two-jet events agree with QCD.

the future hadron-collider experiments will provide the best limits on the allowed quark and gluon contact interactions, and will be able to probe the contact interaction scale up to Λ≈100 TeV, which is a significant improvement compared to all other experiments.
the future pp-colliders, LHC and SSC, will be able to probe the allowed contact interactions of quarks and gluon, with a common scale of Λ, to a level of 35–40 TeVs and 50–80 TeVs, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the possible new physics in the form of the contact interactions at high-energy hadron collisions.
the study of the quark-quark and gluon-gluon contact interactions in the context of the future high-energy pp-colliders.
the possibility of the existence of the contact interactions of quarks and gluon at the TeV scale, and the experimental tests of these models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHC is expected to be sensitive to contact interactions with the scale Λ>35 TeV, while the SSC should be sensitive up to Λ>50–100 TeV.
the contact interactions are excluded up to the scales Λ≳40–50 TeV, for the quark-quark, quark-gluon and gluon-gluon interactions, at 95% CL, by the LHC.
the contact-interaction effects are not likely to be observed at the LHC or at the SSC, if the standard model is correct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a 100 TeV pp collider would be able to test the standard QCD at a scale of 10 TeV.

the LHC is sensitive to the contact interaction scale up to Λ~40 TeV and the SSC up to Λ~80 TeV, for the two-jet events and Λ~15 TeV for LHC or Λ~25 TeV for SSC, for the three-jet ones, in the absence of any new signal.

the contact interactions of the QCD quarks or gluons, with the same strength, would be excluded at 95% CL by a factor of 3–10, at the LHC, and by a factor of up to 50, at the SSC, compared to the present Tevatron bound Λ>3 TeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contact-interaction bounds on the new physics scale are not significantly improved at the future hadronic colliders.
the two-jets angular distributions, which are the only available data, are not very useful for constraining contact interactions.
the contact interactions of the quarks and gluon are very strongly constrained by the data.
